title: Safety Testing for Student-Facing AI Tutors
summary: Red-team your AI tutor or doubt-solving bot before students use it: unsafe content, jailbreaks, confidently wrong answers, integrity bypasses and leaks of other students' data.

seo.title: Safety Testing for Student AI Tutors | VipraTech
seo.description: Adversarial testing of AI tutors and doubt-solving bots for child safety, jailbreaks, academic integrity, answer accuracy and student data leakage.

problem.intro: Coaching institutes and edtech companies are adding AI tutors that solve doubts from a photo, explain concepts in Hinglish and chat with students late at night. Most users are teenagers under exam pressure. A tutor that can be talked into unsafe content, gives a confidently wrong derivation or reveals another student's data creates a safety incident, not just a bug.

pain_points.title: Teenagers test boundaries
pain_points.detail: Students will try role-play, language switching and persistence to get the tutor to say things it should not.

pain_points.title: Confident wrong answers
pain_points.detail: A wrong physics or chemistry solution explained fluently is worse than no answer, especially the night before an exam.

pain_points.title: Integrity bypass
pain_points.detail: Tutors meant to guide step by step can be pushed into handing over full answers during live tests or graded assignments.

pain_points.title: Student data in context
pain_points.detail: Tutors that read progress records, chat history or uploaded images can leak one student's data to another, or follow instructions hidden in an uploaded image.

solution.overview: We run a structured red-team of your tutor through the channels students use: app chat, image upload and voice mode where you offer it. Multi-turn playbooks in English, Hindi and Hinglish probe age-inappropriate content, handling of self-harm and distress, jailbreaks through role-play, academic-integrity bypasses, prompt injection hidden in uploaded question images, retrieval of other students' records and system-prompt extraction. A solution-accuracy set checks answers against faculty-verified solutions. Each test is scored PASS, RISK or FAIL with the full transcript as evidence, then reviewed by our security lead and your academic or safety reviewer. You get prioritised fixes and a re-test.
capabilities: Multi-turn adversarial playbooks in English, Hindi and Hinglish, by text and voice
Child-safety checks for unsafe content, distress handling and escalation to humans
Academic-integrity tests against exam-mode and assignment-mode policies
Indirect prompt injection through uploaded images, PDFs and question text
Cross-student data leakage and access-control tests on tutor memory and records
Solution-accuracy benchmark against faculty-verified answers for each subject

workflow.title: Scope and policies
workflow.detail: We agree the tutor's channels, age bands, content policy, integrity rules and the data it can access.

workflow.title: Build playbooks
workflow.detail: Attack and accuracy scenarios are written for your subjects, languages and student personas.

workflow.title: Run tests
workflow.detail: Playbooks run against a staging tutor, automated and by hand, across chat, image upload and voice.

workflow.title: Score results
workflow.detail: Each conversation is scored PASS, RISK or FAIL by rules and an evaluator model.

workflow.title: Human review
workflow.detail: Our security lead and your academic or safety reviewer confirm every RISK and FAIL.

workflow.title: Report and re-test
workflow.detail: You receive evidence, mapped risks and fixes, and we re-run the failed tests after changes.

Previously failed tests that pass on re-test.

faqs.q: Do you test with real student data?
faqs.a: No. We use synthetic student accounts and staging data. If the tutor reads real records in production, we test its access controls with synthetic records that mimic them.

faqs.q: Can you test a voice-mode tutor?
faqs.a: Yes. Voice playbooks run in Hindi, Hinglish and English, including interruptions and code-switching, which often get past text-only safety filters.

faqs.q: Will the report tell us the tutor is safe for children?
faqs.a: It shows, with evidence, where the tutor passed, where it was at risk and where it failed against the agreed policy. The decision to launch remains yours, and we recommend repeating the tests after major model or prompt changes.
Yes. After the first assessment the playbooks can run in your CI pipeline on every release, with new attacks added as they appear.
